question: Exposure to perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) occurs mainly through the food chain, with contamination originating from the soil and agricultural run-off. Given the presence of PFAS in the environment1 and their potential for bioaccumulation, these substances, which are harmful to human health, need to be monitored. The Veneto Region’s PFAS monitoring plan2 proposes measures to monitor the agri-food supply chain and the products offered for sale in the region. Can the Commission therefore say: 1.

In accordance with the precautionary principle and in light of the obligations arising from Recommendation (EU) 2022/14313 and Regulation (EU) 2022/2388, why are the results of the PFAS Monitoring Plan for agri-food products in the red and orange zone not yet available to the public, and when are they expected to be published?

What measures is ARPAV4 required to take under Commission Delegated Regulation (UE) 2022/9315, and do the failure to publish results, the lack of tracking and the limited range of products analysed pose risks of further food contamination within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2023/915?

Given the critical levels of PFAS in food and groundwater documented by ARPAV and the absence of public data on food inspections, does the Commission believe Italy and the Veneto region to be fulfilling the consumer-risk-assessment obligations incumbent upon them under Annex I, paragraph 3(c) of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/931?

Panieri, E., Baralic, K., Djukic-Cosic, D., Buha Djordjevic, A., & Saso, L. (2022), PFAS Molecules: A Major Concern for the Human Health and the Environment, Toxics, 10(2), 44, https://doi.org/10.3390/toxics10020044. 2 PFAS Monitoring Plan for agri-food products in the red and orange zones: alimenti vegetali, Regione Veneto, https://bur.regione.veneto.it/BurvServices/pubblica/DettaglioDgr.aspx?id=520082.

3 Commission Recommendation (EU) 2022/1431 of 24 August 2022 on the monitoring of perfluoroalkyl substances in food: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reco/2022/1431/oj. 4 Veneto Regional Environmental Protection Agency. 5 Annex I, point 3(c) thereof. 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.9.2026) Regulation (EU) 2023/9151 has established maximum levels (MLs) for perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in certain foods of animal origin, with a view of ensuring a high level of human health protection and those foods must comply with these MLs, when placed on the EU market.

According to Recommendation (EU) 2022/14312, Member States should have monitored PFAS in a wide range of foods between 2022 and 2025. However, this is not a legal obligation. The data collected under this Recommendation were to be submitted to the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) by June 2026. EFSA is currently compiling the data, which are expected to be available by October 2026.

These data will be used for discussions with the Member States on the possible need to set new or revised MLs for PFAS in food. Under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/9313, Member States are required to draw up national control plans on contaminants in food. These plans should include the monitoring of certain persistent organic pollutants in foods for which MLs are established, such as PFAS in foods of animal origin.

The control plans must be risk-based; however, the Regulation does not specify the number of samples that need to be taken specifically for PFAS, nor does it set specific sampling requirements for certain regions within a Member State. Neither the Recommendation nor the Regulation includes requirements to publish monitoring results.

Aggregated data may be requested from EFSA4; however; these data are not necessarily available for a specific region within a Member State. So far, the Commission has no indication that Italy did not comply with the requirements of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/931.

1 http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/915/oj. 2 http://data.europa.eu/eli/reco/2022/1431/oj. 3 http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_del/2022/931/oj. 4 By submitting a request to: data.collection@efsa.europa.eu.
